Management
Under review. Where a community is run. At launch that is its owner alone: Spec 010 section 7 gives both seeing and acting on moderation to the active community owner, and moderators who are not the owner are deferred. Wording on this sheet that says "moderators", and the Moderator section of the app sidebar, describe that later role and at launch mean the owner. It takes over the whole page: the app's own sidebar and bottom navigation are gone while it is open, and a close mark leaves it and returns to the community. It is opened from the community's More menu (Manage) and from the Moderator section of the app sidebar.
Sections, in this order. Moderation: Queue. Community: Profile, Address, Handles, Rules, Links. Safety: AI moderation, Telegram, Assistant. A person sees only the sections they are allowed to use.
On desktop the sections are a sidebar that stays in view, with the close mark and the community at its top, and the chosen section fills the page. On phone the first screen is the list of sections with the close mark; a section opens as its own page with a back arrow and its name centred. A page that opens from a section on the phone is a second column on desktop.
Queue: two lists, Dances and Reports, oldest first, both the owner's alone at launch. For a dance, per the workspace_owner on 2026-09-30: only the community's owner passes or fails it, never the dancer themselves, and the server checks that authority again when the answer is saved. A dance opens full screen, laid out like a feed video with the dancer and song at the bottom left, the dance it is meant to match in the top right corner, and Fail and Pass. The next one opens after a decision and the dancer is told in Notifications. A dance leaves the list unanswered seven days after upload, and the dancer is told it was not reviewed. A report shows the post, what it was reported for and how many times, and Keep and Hide.
AI moderation: every post is checked before it publishes. Six kinds, each set to Allow, Review or Block; a row opens the three choices and the change saves at once. Review sends the post to the Queue. One line lists what is always blocked and cannot be changed.
Telegram: before connecting, one field for the bot's token and Connect. After, the bot, the channel (tap to change), a switch to post new content, a button to share the latest 20 posts, and Disconnect.
Assistant: saving is as built. Every change is a draft and nothing is kept until Save; the page shows Saving, saved, a failure, and the case where the settings changed in another session. Each key saves apart from the draft with its own Check and save. Every built setting is kept: voice replies, the ElevenLabs key, the voice, the voice model, when to reply with voice and the speech characters a day sit on a Voice page. Remembering chats for a day is ours; what OpenRouter, the model's provider and ElevenLabs keep is theirs and is said separately.
Profile, Rules and Links are proposed: the server holds and shows these, with no command to change them. A rule has a title, a body, a report reason, a position and an active or archived status, so its editor has all four fields, moving up and down, and Remove meaning archive. Links are loose data on the server, so name and address are assumed.
Archive is not drawn. The workspace_owner said on 2026-10-12 to do whatever is easiest on the existing API, and the API has no way to archive a community, so the section is left out. That is the design agent's choice and does not settle what archiving would mean. The app still lists Archive with no page.
Address and Handles are on Flows/Community/Address.
The dance check follows the workspace_owner's rulings of 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-09 and is part of launch as of 2026-10-12. The written spec says the first release has no dance grading and no moderator queue for ordinary videos, so the Spec 021 amendment must be ratified before this is built. Ordinary posts still publish by themselves.
To decide: whether a failed dancer may be told why (the 2026-09-30 draft says there is no reviewer note); what a hidden post's author sees; whether six kinds is enough (the app has thirteen, the extra seven being the severe forms); whether Telegram needs the list of what was sent.
To draw: choosing a model and a voice; choosing a Telegram channel; empty lists; hidden posts and restoring one; what someone who is not the owner sees on reaching this page by a link (access denied); a dance nearing its seven days.
Phone: all sections; Queue (dances, one dance, reports, one report); AI moderation; Telegram before and after connecting; Profile; Rules; Links; Assistant, what Save shows, Voice, a key, instructions; editing a rule; editing a link. Dashed means proposed.
The dance rows in Queue show the dancer's handle. That is design only: the moderation contract today lists text posts, comments and replies with an author's profile id, not a public handle, and has no dance queue. The data for these rows is not built.
